title: Send the New Claim Advice Form to the at-fault insurer
why: Day 1: notify the at-fault insurer within 1 working day (GTA 4.1 benchmark) so the hire period is never attacked as unnotified, and start the ICOBS 8.2.6R three-month clock to a reasoned offer or reply.
trigger: Hire or storage has started, or liability has been established against an identified insurer, and no NCAF has been sent.
valueNote: Every unnotified day is a day the insurer will argue it could have mitigated; the NCAF protects the whole hire head.

title: Ask for the handling centre and claim reference
why: Ask on day 1 for the handling centre and reference (GTA 4.2 benchmark: 5 working days) because a payment pack sent to the wrong centre does not start the GTA 6.7 settlement month.
trigger: NCAF sent and no handling reference recorded within 5 working days.

title: Request CCTV, dashcam, witness and police evidence
why: Days 1-7: council and TfL footage is overwritten within weeks, so send preservation requests now; the collision report (Form 518, £215.10) or third-party details (Form 519, £49.00) and independent witness statements decide liability before anyone argues rate.
trigger: Liability is disputed or unclear, or the collision happened where a camera operator (council, TfL, bus, premises) is likely to hold footage, within 7 days of the collision.
valueNote: A liability loss wipes out every head; evidence costing £49-£215 protects the whole file and the Tescher costs exposure.

title: Reply in writing to the insurer's replacement-vehicle offer
why: An unanswered intervention offer is the mitigation argument the insurer wants (Copley v Lawn; Sayce v TNT): reply within 1 working day with reasons, asking for the terms and cost of the offer, and log it in the intervention register.
trigger: An intervention offer (replacement vehicle, repair, or payment) is logged with no written reply.
valueNote: Silence caps damages at the insurer's own cost of a car; a reasoned reply keeps the full hire head alive.

title: Collect the Statement of Means and three months of bank statements
why: Impecuniosity is pleaded and proved by the claimant (Diriye v Bojaj; Zurich v Umerji), so collect the Statement of Means, all bank and credit-card statements and available credit at sign-up, before the insurer asks and before any unless order.
trigger: Hire at a rate above the basic hire rate with the impecuniosity gate not satisfied.
valueNote: The gap between credit hire and BHR is the whole margin on the hire head; without this evidence the file is a BHR file.

title: Close the enforceability gap in the hire agreement
why: An unenforceable agreement means no loss (Dimond v Lovell; W v Veolia; Salat v Barutis): serve the Schedule 2 information and Schedule 3 cancellation form, obtain the written express request to start, and keep the credit within RAO art 60F (12 payments, 12 months, no charges).
trigger: Enforceability gate shows a missing Sch 2 pack, Sch 3 form, express request to start or signed audit certificate.
valueNote: The insurer looks here first because it costs them nothing and can zero the hire; look first ourselves.

title: Collect-or-pay notice for a stored total-loss vehicle
why: Storage is the first head an insurer caps: once the vehicle is a total loss, put the insurer on written notice to collect the salvage or pay storage from a stated date (GTA 4.14 benchmark on off-hire after total-loss payment), so the clock on storage is theirs, not ours.
trigger: Vehicle assessed as a total loss (or engineer's report issued) while in storage and no collect-or-pay notice has been sent.
valueNote: Live-file lesson: storage capped at report + 48h when no notice was sent.

title: Send a repair-delay notice (GTA 4.10/4.11 benchmark)
why: Where the repair or settlement is delayed by 2 working days or more than 20% over the estimate, tell the insurer in writing with the cause (parts, authority, payment), because a dated chronology of insurer-caused delay is what wins the period argument (Mattocks v Mann).
trigger: Monitoring diary shows a delay of 2+ working days or more than 20% against the estimated repair period, or no authorisation within 3 working days.

title: End the hire: an off-hire trigger has fired
why: Hire must stop when the trigger fires (repair complete and vehicle ready for collection plus 24 hours; cash in lieu received; total-loss payment received; 1 working day termination notice): every day past the trigger is unrecoverable and is the easiest cut the insurer makes.
trigger: Repair completion, cash-in-lieu payment, total-loss payment or termination notice logged while a hire is still open.
valueNote: Live-file lesson: hire and storage ran past the trigger and the excess days were lost.

title: Send the clean payment pack the day hire ends
why: The settlement month (GTA 6.7 benchmark) runs from a clean pack reaching the correct handling centre: covering letter, Mitigation Questionnaire with statement of truth, Advice Form, Hire Period Validation Form, engineer's report, storage and recovery accounts. A pack missing one item restarts the clock.
trigger: Hire ended and no payment pack sent, with the payment-pack validator reporting complete.
valueNote: Debtor days start here; nothing is owed on a benchmark basis until the pack is clean.

title: Split the heads: demand payment of undisputed heads and an interim payment
why: Dispute hire separately: PAV, recovery and storage that are not challenged should be paid now (ICOBS 8.1 prompt handling), with an interim payment requested and, if litigated, applied for under CPR Part 25 Section V on the admitted heads.
trigger: Insurer disputes one head (usually hire) while other heads are admitted or unanswered more than 14 days after the pack.
valueNote: Cash conversion: a paid PAV at day 20 beats a contested global settlement at day 120.

title: Day 7 chaser to the handler
why: Chase at day 7 with the pack date, the amount and the GTA 6.7 month end stated, so the file shows a prompt-handling trail (ICOBS 8.1.1R) and the late-payment benchmark dates are on the record.
trigger: 7 calendar days after the payment pack with no payment or reasoned reply.

title: Day 14 chaser to the team leader
why: Escalate at day 14 to the team leader, repeating the figures and asking for the handler's reasoned position on each head (ICOBS 8.2.6R), because a later complaint needs to show the firm was given the chance to put it right.
trigger: 14 calendar days after the payment pack with no payment or reasoned reply.

title: Day 21 chaser to the claims manager
why: Escalate at day 21 to the claims manager, warning that a DISP complaint follows at day 28 and that late-payment additions (10% from day 31, 20% from day 61, GTA 6.8.6, quoted as an industry benchmark) and interest will be added to the schedule.
trigger: 21 calendar days after the payment pack with no payment or reasoned reply.

title: Formal complaint to the insurer under DISP 1 at day 28
why: At day 28 send a formal complaint citing ICOBS 8.1 and 8.2: the firm must give a final response within eight weeks (DISP 1.6.2R) and complaints are costed and reported, which moves files that chasers do not. Do not threaten the FOS: a third-party claimant is not an eligible complainant against the at-fault insurer (DISP 2.7.6R).
trigger: 28 calendar days after the payment pack with no payment or reasoned reply, after the day 7/14/21 chasers.
forumCheck: FORUM_NOT_OPEN: third-party claimant vs at-fault insurer cannot be referred to the FOS; the complaint route ends at the firm's final response and the next step is pre-action correspondence and court.

title: DSAR to the insurer for call recordings and claim notes
why: Where the insurer alleges an ignored offer or a late notification, a subject access request (UK GDPR Art 15, one month) for the call recordings, claim notes and intervention logs tests the allegation; the insurer must have a complaints process before any ICO complaint (DUAA 2025 s.103).
trigger: Insurer asserts an intervention offer, an ignored call or a late notification that the register does not show.
valueNote: Free, one statutory month, and it costs the insurer compliance resource; the recording usually ends the argument.

title: Add ICOBS 8.2.9R interest (base + 4%) to the schedule
why: If the insurer has made no reasoned offer within three months of a fully quantified claim, ICOBS 8.2.9R-8.2.11R requires it to pay simple interest at Bank of England base rate plus 4% from the date the offer was due; put it on the schedule now and claim s.69 CCA 1984 interest in the alternative at court.
trigger: Three months have run from a fully quantified claim to a UK-authorised motor insurer with no reasoned offer or reply.
valueNote: Interest is free money and it is routinely omitted; the ICOBS rate is a rule, not a GTA benchmark.

title: Letter before claim (Practice Direction on Pre-Action Conduct)
why: A compliant letter of claim with the schedule, the documents relied on and a 14-30 day response period is the gateway to issue and to costs consequences; drafted for the claimant as litigant in person or an instructed solicitor to sign, because conduct of litigation is reserved (LSA 2007 s.12).
trigger: Final response received or eight weeks expired with the claim unpaid, or the complaint route is not worth the delay.
valueNote: Check limitation (6 years tort) and the costs exposure before the letter goes: a weak-liability hire-heavy file is a Tescher file.

title: Claimant's Part 36 offer at issue
why: A claimant's Part 36 offer pitched at the realistic settlement figure puts the costs and enhanced-interest consequences of CPR 36.17 on the insurer from day 21 (the fixed-costs regime of Part 45 and the small claims costs rules in 27.14 limit but do not remove the pressure).
trigger: Claim issued (or letter before claim sent) and no Part 36 offer on the record.
valueNote: Write the walk-away number down before the offer; a number decided mid-call is a worse number.

title: Request default judgment when no acknowledgment or defence is filed
why: If the insurer files no acknowledgment of service within 14 days of service of the particulars, or no defence within 28 days after acknowledging, the claimant may request default judgment under CPR 12.3 (form N225 for a specified sum); the request is the claimant's as litigant in person, and a set-aside under CPR 13 is the insurer's problem.
trigger: Claim served and the acknowledgment or defence deadline has passed with nothing filed.
notes: No CCGUK template: the request is HMCTS form N225/N227, completed and filed by the claimant (or solicitor). bundle.litigation_index records what was served and when.

title: Send the vendor verification pack so payment is not bounced
why: Insurers pay only a validated payee: send the bank letter on bank letterhead, the certificate of incorporation (17430389), proof of registered office and a director ID, with the account in the exact registered name 'Courtesy Cars Group UK Ltd' so Confirmation of Payee returns a full match. Never send legacy details.
trigger: First claim against an insurer not yet holding CCGUK's vendor record, or a payment rejected as 'bank details could not be validated'.
valueNote: Live-file lesson (File 1): a trading-name mismatch cost weeks of debtor days on an agreed sum.

title: Refer any injury element to a solicitor, no fee
why: Personal injury is regulated claims management activity and referral fees are banned (LASPO 2012 ss.56-60; RAO arts 89G-89M): route the injury to a solicitor at intake without a fee and keep the damage-only claim here. Limitation for injury is 3 years (Limitation Act 1980 s.11).
trigger: Any party reports injury at FNOL or later.
notes: No CCGUK template: the referral is a logged task and a call to the panel solicitor; no document goes to the insurer about injury.
forumCheck: PERIMETER: carrying on regulated claims management activity without FCA authorisation is an offence (FSMA s.19); no fee, no advice on the injury head.

title: Offer the held replacement car to the client
why: Autopilot hire.offer: the held car is offered with a like-for-like explanation, by email from the Claims Team.
trigger: A car is held for the claim and no offer has been sent.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Confirm the booking once the client accepts
why: Autopilot hire.confirm: the held car is confirmed and the agreement number allocated.
trigger: The client accepted the hire offer and the booking is still only held.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Book the delivery and tell the client
why: Autopilot hire.delivery: a delivery slot in business hours, confirmed to the client in writing.
trigger: The booking is confirmed and no delivery is planned or the client has not been told.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Prepare the hire-start paperwork for the owner to approve
why: Pre-contract information, the Sch 3 cancellation form and the express request must be given before the hire starts (W v Veolia).
trigger: The booking is confirmed and the hire-start pack is not yet approved.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Prepare the sign-up pack for the owner to approve
why: The client signs the letter of authority and the accident report before the services start.
trigger: The claim is accepted and the sign-up pack is not yet approved.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Chase unsigned paperwork
why: Unsigned paperwork leaves the hire unenforceable; chase after 2 and 5 days, call after 7.
trigger: Paperwork was sent for signature and has not come back.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Tell the at-fault insurer the hire has started
why: The insurer is told of the hire within 1 working day so it cannot say it was kept in the dark.
trigger: A hire started and the at-fault insurer has not been told.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Instruct the independent engineer
why: An early inspection fixes the repair period that the hire depends on.
trigger: Services are agreed and no engineer has been instructed.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Arrange recovery and storage of the client’s car
why: A car that cannot be driven is recovered and secured; storage is kept short.
trigger: The client’s car cannot be driven and is not yet recovered.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Book the collection of the hire car
why: The hire ends on the off-hire deadline; the collection is booked for it.
trigger: An off-hire trigger was recorded and no collection is planned.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Prepare the invoices and the claimed ledger rows
why: Invoices and ledger rows are prepared by the autopilot and written only on the owner’s approval.
trigger: Every hire and storage period has ended and no billing pack is approved.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Pay the client what is theirs (PAV, excess)
why: Money held for the client is paid on promptly; the owner pays it.
trigger: A PAV or excess payment was received that belongs to the client.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Close the file
why: Closing a file is the owner’s decision; the closure letter is prepared for the client.
trigger: Every head is paid, settled or written off and the car is back.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Check the client’s need for a replacement car
why: Need is the first thing an insurer attacks; it is recorded in the client’s own words.
trigger: Hire needs are missing or the need is weak.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.

title: Check the driver can be insured on our cars
why: Uninsured driving is a hard stop; referrals go to the owner with evidence.
trigger: The driver profile is incomplete or the driver needs a referral.
notes: Autopilot step code (SUPREME-AUTOPILOT §A.3): raised by the Autopilot plan, not by the nextActions engine.
